_comment: 议题投票数据。candidates=未辩候选(供投票)，debated=已辩(链到辩论)。投票免 GitHub 登录，存于自建后端(Cloudflare Worker + D1，见 ~/Desktop/cissy0802.github.io/engage-backend/)：每候选一个 poll，key='topic:'+id，choice up/down，净票=👍−👎。votes 字段由 routine 每次跑 `python3 refresh_votes.py`(读后端 /votes-net) 回写；页面 ideas.js 也会实时拉取覆盖显示。观众自提议题在评论 page='thinker-open-questions'，各候选下讨论 page='topic:'+id——routine 读这些把好提案提炼成新 candidates。新候选加进 candidates 即可。

candidates.q: 专业人士能因信念拒绝服务吗？
candidates.q_en: May a professional refuse to serve on grounds of conscience?
candidates.note: 医生拒绝执行、药剂师拒绝配药、面包师拒绝接单——同一条「良心自由」用在不同人身上，我们的直觉常常相反。允许拒绝，偏远处的权利形同虚设；不许拒绝，成本落到最难说不的人身上。判据该是什么？
candidates.note_en: A doctor who won't perform a procedure, a pharmacist who won't dispense, a baker who won't take the order: the same 'freedom of conscience' draws opposite intuitions depending on who invokes it. Allow refusal and rights go hollow wherever staff are scarce; forbid it and the cost lands on whoever is least able to say no. What should decide it?

candidates.q: 旅行者来了之后，当地人得到了什么？
candidates.q_en: When the travellers arrive, what do the locals get?
candidates.note: 民宿抽走长租房、老街按游客口味重做、旺季本地人自己出不了门——旅游的收入和代价，从不落在同一批人身上。旅行者有没有义务知道自己的分量？限度该由市场、政府，还是住在那里的人来定？
candidates.note_en: Short-lets drain the rental market, old streets get remade to visitors' taste, locals can't leave home in peak season: tourism's income and its costs never land on the same people. Do travellers owe it to know their own weight? Who should set the limit: the market, the government, or the people who live there?

candidates.q: 「适者生存」能用来解释社会吗？
candidates.q_en: Can 'survival of the fittest' explain society?
candidates.note: 社会和市场里确实有类似「优胜劣汰」的机制，可由此推出「不该救助弱者」，就是从「是」跳到了「应该」——何况达尔文本人认为同情出自社会本能。把一个选择说成规律，做决定的人就从句子里消失了。
candidates.note_en: Society and markets do have something like selection. But concluding 'so we shouldn't help the weak' leaps from is to ought, and Darwin himself traced sympathy to our social instincts. Recast a choice as a law of nature and the person making it vanishes from the sentence.

candidates.q: 一条老规矩，什么时候该改？
candidates.q_en: When should an old rule be changed?
candidates.note: 守多久算固执，改多快算随波逐流？切斯特顿说，看不出篱笆为什么立着就先别拆；可有些篱笆的立法者早已不在，要防的野兽也早绝迹。难处始终是：谁来判定哪一条是根本，这个判定又归谁管？
candidates.note_en: How long is steadfast before it turns stubborn, how fast is reform before it becomes drift? Chesterton said not to pull down a fence until you know why it stands, but some fences have outlived their builders and the beasts they kept out. The hard part: who decides which rules are fundamental, and who oversees that decision?

candidates.q: 让人不舒服的好东西，卖得出去吗？
candidates.q_en: Can something good that makes people uncomfortable survive a market?
candidates.note: 如实的体检报告、不讨好的新闻、会让人挂科的课、直言的朋友——它们的价值恰恰来自那点不适，可供给者靠的是对方愿不愿意再来。市场于是把不适磨平。有没有别的办法养活它们？
candidates.note_en: An honest check-up, unflattering news, a course you can fail, a friend who tells you straight: their value lies in the discomfort, yet whoever supplies them depends on you coming back. So markets sand the discomfort away. Is there another way to keep them alive?

candidates.q: 家里那件不许提的事，该挑开吗？
candidates.q_en: Should the thing a family never mentions be opened up?
candidates.note: 几乎每个家庭都有一两件所有人都知道、没人开口的事。沉默常是为了保护人，可被遮住的事对下一代的影响，往往比事件本身更大。挑开它的最低条件是什么？有些沉默，是不是让一家人还能同桌吃饭的体面？
candidates.note_en: Almost every family has a thing or two that everyone knows and no one says. Silence often protects, yet what stays hidden can shape the next generation more than the event itself. What are the minimum conditions for bringing it into the open? And is some silence the decency that lets a family keep sharing a table?

candidates.q: 自己管住自己，是成熟还是驯服？
candidates.q_en: Keeping yourself in line: maturity, or domestication?
candidates.note: 当约束已经搬进心里，连照妖镜都分不出真心与二心——从外面看，真受了规训的人和只学会表演规训的人是同一个样子。还能发声、只是不再单方面离场，算成熟；连「这次是你错了」都听不见了，算驯服？
candidates.note_en: Once the constraint has moved inside, not even the demon-revealing mirror can tell the true heart from the second one: from outside, someone truly disciplined and someone who has only learned to perform discipline look the same. Still able to speak up, just no longer walking out alone: maturity. No longer able to hear 'this time you're wrong': domestication?
candidates.brief: 副标题：当约束已经搬进心里，连照妖镜都分不出真心与二心，人还能怎么自查？　引子用西游记第五十八回：回目「二心搅乱大乾坤，一体难修真寂灭」，六耳猕猴正是悟空的另一半心。这一回的机关在于谁分不出——观音的慧眼、照妖镜、整个天庭都分不出，只有如来分得清，等于说：从外面看，真的受了规训的人与只是学会表演规训的人是同一个样子，任何制度性的检测工具都失效。更要紧的是分工：如来只用金钵盂把它扣住，一棒打死是悟空自己动的手，如来「不忍」，书里还补「至今绝此一种」——刑罚在外面的时候叫紧箍，等看守搬进屋里就不需要刑罚了，所以到灵山箍自己掉了：不是因为自由了，是因为它没活可干了。还有一处精确化：六耳要的不是「不去取经」，它另立一队自己去取经——被打死的不是叛逃的欲望，是署名权，这也解释了为什么这种改变不痛苦。　正方最硬的论证：悟空在此之前已经证明过一次，齐天大圣神通盖世，却在任何需要持续十四年的事上完全无能，代价是五百年压山；他此后获得的是忍受冤枉、拖累与反复被赶走的能力，这是一切需要时间的好东西的前提。而且他没变听话——照样打妖怪、挖苦八戒、跟师父吵；被杀掉的只是「会走出去的那一面」。孔子「七十而从心所欲不逾矩」是这一版的最强表述：约束被消化到不再是约束。　反方最硬的论证：六耳的本事书里写明是善聆音、能察理、知前后——全是辨识能力，被打死的恰恰是那个能看出「这次师父真的错了」的部分（而这一次师父确实错了，贬书是不公的）；此后悟空的判断再没一次被允许压过唐僧，取经队伍靠「眼力更差的一方永远赢得争论」往前走。且如来已把它扣住，招安是现成的选项——整部书的方法论就是收服，只有这一个被绝了种。　可能的落点：判据不看约束的多少，看那一面是被收编还是被处死——还能发声、只是不再有单方面离场的权力叫成熟；异议源被关掉、再也收不到「这次是你错了」的信号叫驯服。照妖镜失效那一层意味着这事只能内查，没有外部判据。　选角方向：傅柯（规训内化、无需刑罚的服从）、弗洛姆（逃避自由与积极自由）、荣格（阴影：压下去的不会消失，只换出口）、尼采（骆驼—狮子—小孩）、孔子（从心所欲不逾矩，正方）、庄子（不受规训那一面自有其用）、爱比克泰德或阿德勒（自愿的纪律）。　与已辩过的不重叠：escape-from-freedom 问人怕不怕自由，progress-liberation-or-control 问进步是解放还是控制，being-yourself 问有没有本真的我，本题只问「约束已经内化之后怎么分辨成熟与驯服」。
candidates.brief_en: Subtitle: once the restraint has moved inside, and not even a demon-revealing mirror can tell a true mind from a divided one, what is left to check yourself against? The entry point is chapter 58 of Journey to the West, whose own title reads 'two minds throw the great cosmos into disorder; as one body, true quiescence is hard to attain' — the Six-Eared Macaque is Wukong's other half. The device of the chapter is who cannot tell them apart: Guanyin's eye, the demon-revealing mirror and the whole celestial bureaucracy all fail; only the Buddha can. Which is to say: from outside, a person who has genuinely internalised discipline and one who has merely learnt to perform it look identical, and every institutional instrument of detection fails. More telling still is the division of labour — the Buddha only pins the creature under his golden bowl; the killing blow is Wukong's own, the Buddha 'cannot bear it', and the text adds that the species has been extinct ever since. While punishment is still outside it is called the headband; once the guard has moved indoors, punishment becomes unnecessary — which is why the band falls off by itself at the end: not because he is free, but because it has no work left to do. One precision often missed: the Macaque did not want to abandon the pilgrimage; it assembled its own party and set out west alone. What was killed is not the urge to defect but authorship — which is also why the change is painless. The strongest case for maturity: Wukong had already run the experiment once; peerless in power, he was wholly incapable of anything requiring fourteen continuous years, and paid five hundred years under a mountain. What he gains afterwards is the capacity to endure an unjust master, a burdensome companion and repeated expulsion — the precondition of every good thing that takes time. And he does not become docile: he still fights demons, still mocks Bajie, still argues with his master. What was killed was precisely 'the part that walks out'. Confucius's 'at seventy I could follow my heart's desire without transgressing the bounds' is this position at its strongest: restraint digested until it is no longer restraint. The strongest case for domestication: the Macaque's gifts are spelled out as hearing all sounds, discerning reason, knowing what came before and after — faculties of discernment. What was killed is exactly the part that could see that the master was wrong this time (and he was: the expulsion was unjust). Never again is Wukong's judgement allowed to override his master's, and the pilgrimage proceeds by the less perceptive party always winning the argument. The Buddha had it pinned; conversion was available — conversion is the method of the entire book, and this is the only creature wiped out instead. A possible landing point: judge not the amount of restraint but whether that side was annexed or executed. Still able to speak, merely stripped of the power to walk out unilaterally, is maturity; the channel of dissent closed, so that the signal 'this time you are the one who is wrong' never arrives, is domestication. And because the mirror fails, this can only be checked from inside. Casting: Foucault (internalised discipline, obedience without punishment), Fromm (escape from freedom versus positive freedom), Jung (the shadow: what is pushed down does not vanish, it changes its exit), Nietzsche (camel, lion, child), Confucius (following the heart within bounds, for the affirmative), Zhuangzi (the undisciplined side has its own use), Epictetus or Adler (voluntary discipline). Distinct from what has already been debated: escape-from-freedom asks whether people fear freedom, progress-liberation-or-control asks whether progress liberates or controls, being-yourself asks whether there is an authentic self; this one asks only how, once restraint is internalised, maturity is told apart from domestication.

candidates.q: 城市该规划出来，还是让它自己长？
candidates.q_en: Should a city be planned, or left to grow?
candidates.note: 柯布西耶要推平老街、建光辉城市，雅各布斯说街上的眼睛才是安全；斯科特则认为，让国家「看得清」的规划，恰恰抹掉了真实生活的秩序。城市更像机器，还是更像生物？
candidates.note_en: Le Corbusier wanted to raze old streets for a Radiant City; Jane Jacobs said the eyes on the street are what keep it safe; James Scott argued that planning which makes a city legible to the state erases the order real life had built. Is a city more like a machine or an organism?

candidates.q: 公地悲剧，只能靠私有或国管吗？
candidates.q_en: Is the tragedy of the commons solved only by private property or the state?
candidates.note: 哈丁说公共资源注定被耗尽，解法只有私有化或政府管。奥斯特罗姆在瑞士牧场、尼泊尔水渠、缅因龙虾渔场里找到了第三条路：没有中心的社区自治。它靠什么撑住，又在什么规模上失灵？
candidates.note_en: Hardin said shared resources are doomed to exhaustion unless privatised or run by the state. In Swiss pastures, Nepali canals and Maine lobster grounds, Elinor Ostrom found a third way: self-governing communities with no centre. What holds them together, and at what scale do they fail?

candidates.q: 生命和非生命的界线在哪？
candidates.q_en: Where is the line between living and non-living?
candidates.note: 病毒离开宿主就像一粒晶体，它算活着吗？薛定谔说生命以负熵为食，马图拉纳说生命是能不断生产自己的系统，佛学十二因缘则不承认有一个「活着的主体」。这条线是自然划的，还是我们划的？
candidates.note_en: A virus outside a host behaves like a crystal: is it alive? Schrödinger said life feeds on negative entropy; Maturana defined it as a system that keeps producing itself; the Buddhist chain of dependent origination denies there is any 'living subject' at all. Is this line drawn by nature, or by us?

candidates.q: 疼痛是身体在报警，还是大脑在预测？
candidates.q_en: Is pain the body's alarm, or the brain's prediction?
candidates.note: 幻肢会痛，安慰剂能止痛，慢性痛常常找不到伤口——痛似乎不只是伤处传来的信号，而是大脑的推断。佛陀说第一支箭难免，第二支是自己射的。若痛有一部分是预测出来的，能不能被改写？
candidates.note_en: Phantom limbs hurt, placebos relieve pain, chronic pain often has no wound to show: pain seems less a signal from the injury than an inference by the brain. The Buddha said the first arrow can't be avoided, but the second we fire ourselves. If part of pain is predicted, can it be rewritten?

candidates.q: 越想要越得不到的东西，该怎么要？
candidates.q_en: How do you pursue what pursuit drives away?
candidates.note: 睡眠、灵感、自然、被爱、幸福——越用力越远。埃尔斯特把它们叫作「本质上只能是副产品的状态」，道家讲无为，禅讲不求，失眠的人最懂反弹。既然不能直接追，还能做点什么，又该停在哪里？
candidates.note_en: Sleep, inspiration, spontaneity, being loved, happiness: the harder you try, the further they slip. Jon Elster called them 'states that are essentially by-products'; Daoists speak of non-action, Zen of not seeking, and insomniacs know the rebound best. If you can't chase them directly, what can you do, and where should you stop?

candidates.q: 说不清原理的「有效」，算不算知识？
candidates.q_en: Does 'it works' without knowing why count as knowledge?
candidates.note: 柳树皮止痛早于阿司匹林几千年，老中医、民间方子、老师傅的经验都说得出「管用」却说不出为什么。没有机制解释的有效，是迷信，还是还没被翻译的知识？反过来，有一套漂亮机制却不见效的，又算什么？
candidates.note_en: Willow bark eased pain thousands of years before aspirin; traditional doctors, folk remedies and old craftsmen can say 'it works' without saying why. Is efficacy without a mechanism superstition, or knowledge not yet translated? And what of elegant mechanisms that don't actually work?

candidates.q_en: What is music for, in survival terms?
candidates.note: 平克说音乐是「听觉芝士蛋糕」，演化上可有可无；也有人说它是求偶信号，或比语言更早的群体黏合剂。儒家把乐放进治国，叔本华说音乐直通意志本身。人为什么会在没有任何好处的地方，一起唱歌？
candidates.note_en: Steven Pinker called music 'auditory cheesecake', an evolutionary extra; others see a courtship signal, or a social glue older than language. Confucians put music at the heart of government; Schopenhauer said it speaks directly of the will itself. Why do people sing together where nothing seems to be gained?

candidates.q: 组织该听最响的声音吗？
candidates.q_en: Should an organisation listen to the loudest voice?
candidates.note: 开口要的人往往拿得多：他送来了信息，也让「拒绝」变贵了。可哭换来的多是预算、例外这类一次性的东西，换不来信任与托付；同样的哭，不同的人付出的代价也不同。组织若按谁最让人头疼来分资源，留下来的会是谁？
candidates.note_en: Those who ask tend to get more: they bring information, and they make saying no more costly. But complaining mostly wins one-off things like budget and exceptions, not trust or responsibility, and the same complaint costs different people very different amounts. If an organisation hands out resources to whoever causes the most headaches, who ends up staying?

candidates.q: 让人害怕，能把组织管好吗？
candidates.q_en: Can fear make an organisation run well?
candidates.note: 怕被追责，人就不越红线；也正因为怕，坏消息被压下、错误被藏起、没人敢试新东西。问责和提心吊胆的界线在哪：是规则事先说清、惩罚可以预期，还是全看上面的脸色？自检：你的团队上一次主动上报自己的失误，是什么时候？
candidates.note_en: Fear of blame keeps people from crossing red lines; the same fear gets bad news buried, mistakes hidden and new ideas left untried. Where is the line between accountability and walking on eggshells: rules set out in advance and penalties you can predict, or everything hanging on the boss's mood? A test: when did someone on your team last report their own mistake unprompted?

candidates.q: 把功劳让出去，会越让越多吗？
candidates.q_en: Does giving away credit bring more of it back?
candidates.note: 大方归功于人，换来信任、合作和口碑；可这要有人看见你在让。在按署名记账、名额有限的评审里，没人看见的让功就是白让，而资深者让是锦上添花，新人让可能就此隐身。自检：在你那里，让功的人是吃亏还是得益？
candidates.note_en: Crediting others generously earns trust, cooperation and a good name, but only if someone sees you doing it. In reviews that count bylines and have fixed quotas, unseen generosity is simply lost; a senior person giving credit away gains polish, a junior one may vanish. A test: where you work, do those who share credit lose out or come out ahead?

candidates.q: 内卷，一个人退得出来吗？
candidates.q_en: Can one person step out of the rat race?
candidates.note: 人人多卷一点，名次不变、大家更累，是典型的负和。可单方面停下，往往只是让自己垫底。出路在个人清醒、小圈子约定，还是只能等规则改？躺平是看透，还是另一种认输？自检：你正在卷的那件事，如果所有人同时停下，你会损失什么？
candidates.note_en: When everyone pushes a little harder, the rankings stay the same and everyone is more worn out: a classic negative-sum game. Yet stopping on your own usually just puts you at the bottom. Is the way out personal clarity, a pact within a small circle, or only a change in the rules? Is lying flat seeing through it, or another way of giving up? A test: if everyone stopped the race you are in at the same moment, what would you lose?

debated.q: 幸福到底是什么？我们是否应该追求幸福？
debated.q_en: What is happiness, really? And should we even pursue it?

debated.q: AI 时代，人如何夺回注意力与存在的意义？
debated.q_en: In the age of AI, how do we reclaim our attention and the meaning of our existence?

debated.q: AI 取代人类工作后，会有『存在危机』吗？
debated.q_en: After AI replaces human work, will we face an 'existential crisis'?

debated.q: 原生家庭的创伤，能真正走出来吗？
debated.q_en: Can we truly move past the trauma of the family we're born into?

debated.q: AI 与算法：在增强我们，还是在让我们退化？
debated.q_en: AI and algorithms: are they augmenting us, or making us atrophy?

debated.q: AI 时代该怎么养孩子？——拼命鸡娃、挤名校到底还值不值得？
debated.q_en: Raising kids in the age of AI: is intense “tiger parenting” and chasing elite schools still worth it?

debated.q: 科技大厂的『扁平化』——一个经理带 30–50 人，会成为常态吗？
debated.q_en: Big-tech 'flattening' — one manager over 30–50 reports: is this the new normal?

debated.q: 是否有“造物主”，如果有的话，TA为什么要造出人类？
debated.q_en: Is there a 'Creator'? And if so, why would they have made humankind?

debated.q: 一个好的『管理者』，到底是怎样的？
debated.q_en: What actually makes a good manager?

debated.q: 『知道』和『做到』之间，差在哪？
debated.q_en: Where does the gap between knowing and doing come from?

debated.q: 人是否应该追求长生，如果人真的能够长生，世界会怎样？
debated.q_en: Should we pursue immortality — and if humans really could live forever, what would the world become?

debated.q: 金钱能（在多大程度上）买到幸福？
debated.q_en: Can money buy happiness — and how much?

debated.q: 「只专注你能控制的」，是智慧还是逃避？
debated.q_en: 'Focus only on what you can control' — wisdom, or escape?

debated.q: 年轻人为什么不想生孩子了？
debated.q_en: Why don't young people want children anymore?

debated.q: 我们该如何面对死亡？如何做到「向死而生」？
debated.q_en: How should we face death — and how do we actually live 'toward' it (being-toward-death)?

debated.q: 为什么这一代人越来越难谈恋爱？
debated.q_en: Why is this generation finding it ever harder to date?

debated.q: 儒、释、道的异同：三家分歧究竟在哪，又在何处殊途同归？
debated.q_en: Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism: where do the three traditions truly differ, and where do they converge?

debated.q: 普通人投资，该买大盘指数，还是买自己拿着放心的个股？
debated.q_en: For ordinary investors: buy the broad index, or the individual stocks you can hold with confidence?

debated.q: 靠恐惧驱动的优秀，该不该放下？
debated.q_en: Should we let go of excellence driven by fear?

debated.q: 东方与西方哲学，源头何以不同？
debated.q_en: Why did Eastern and Western philosophy diverge at the source?

debated.q: 『组织政治』是毒瘤，还是必需？
debated.q_en: Is 'office politics' a tumor, or a necessity?

debated.q: 家中老人病重、靠插管维持近乎植物人的状态，作为子女，该不该撤管放手？
debated.q_en: An elderly parent kept alive by tubes in a near-vegetative state — should the children withdraw life support and let go?

debated.q: 企业用人，该「以德为先」还是「以才为先」？
debated.q_en: When a company hires and promotes, should it put character first, or ability first?

debated.q: 下属不行，该带教还是该换人？
debated.q_en: When a subordinate falls short: coach, or move them out?

debated.q: 「你眼中的别人，其实是你自己」？
debated.q_en: 'The others you see are really you' — is that true?

debated.q: 世俗意义上的『成功』——财富、地位、名声、成就——到底值不值得追求？
debated.q_en: Is worldly 'success' — wealth, status, fame, achievement — worth pursuing at all?

debated.q: 「忠于真实的自我」是不是个伪命题？到底有没有一个本真的我？
debated.q_en: Is 'being true to your authentic self' a false premise — and is there even an authentic self to begin with?

debated.q: 什么样的不平等是可以接受的？
debated.q_en: What kind of inequality is acceptable?

debated.q: 我们的成功与失败，多少是「应得的」？努力真能决定命运吗？
debated.q_en: How much of our success or failure do we actually deserve — and does effort really decide our fate?

debated.q: 该不该用基因编辑「设计」更聪明、更健康的下一代？
debated.q_en: Should we use gene editing to 'design' smarter, healthier children?

debated.q: 父母年迈失能，该亲自接回家照顾，还是送养老院、请护工？
debated.q_en: When parents grow old and frail, should you care for them at home yourself, or place them in a nursing home and hire professional carers?

debated.q: 该频繁跳槽，还是在一处深耕固守？
debated.q_en: Should you job-hop often, or stay put and dig deep in one place?

debated.q: 生产力一次次飞跃，人更闲了还是更忙了？
debated.q_en: With each leap in productivity, are we more leisured or busier?

debated.q: 一样东西的价值，到底由什么决定？（劳动、效用、稀缺，还是别的？）
debated.q_en: What ultimately determines the value of a thing? (Labor, utility, scarcity — or something else?)

debated.q: AI 创造的财富，会让社会更不平等吗？
debated.q_en: Will the wealth AI creates make society more unequal?

debated.q: 想改变自己，该先立身份还是先放下自我？
debated.q_en: To change yourself: build an identity first, or let the self go?

debated.q: 人是否拥有真正的自由意志？
debated.q_en: Do humans have genuine free will?

debated.q: 是地理塑造了思想，还是思想自有其命？
debated.q_en: Did geography shape thought, or do ideas have a life of their own?

debated.q: 想活得不后悔，该入世还是出世？
debated.q_en: To live without regret: engage the world, or withdraw from it?

debated.q: 为什么我们忍不住跟别人比？嫉妒能消除吗？
debated.q_en: Why can't we stop comparing ourselves to others — and can envy ever be cured?

debated.q: 如果有了足够的钱（财务自由），是否还应该继续工作？
debated.q_en: If you had enough money to never need to, should you still work?

debated.q: 量子物理是否说明「观测」真的改变了世界？
debated.q_en: Does quantum physics show that 'observation' really changes the world?

debated.q: AI 时代，人的心智该往「深」练还是往「广」练？——不受打扰的深度专注，还是驾驭多线程的调度与切换？
debated.q_en: In the AI era, should the mind train for depth or breadth — undistracted deep focus, or orchestrating and switching across many threads?

debated.q: 品德是教出来的，还是长出来的？——美德到底可不可教？
debated.q_en: Can virtue be taught — is character instilled, or does it grow on its own?

debated.q: 普通人该进大厂求稳，还是闯小公司、创业？
debated.q_en: Should you join a big company for stability, or take a startup — or strike out on your own?

debated.q: 贫富差距本身会让人生病吗？——该不该把不平等当成一个公共健康问题？
debated.q_en: Does the wealth gap itself make people sick — and should inequality be treated as a public-health problem?

debated.q: 教育到底是为了什么——筛选人才的机器，还是培养人的土壤？
debated.q_en: What is education actually for — a machine to sort talent, or soil to cultivate a person?

debated.q: AI 时代，该练流体智力还是晶体智力？
debated.q_en: In the age of AI: train fluid intelligence, or crystallized?

debated.q: 数学是被发现的，还是被发明的？
debated.q_en: Is mathematics discovered, or invented?

debated.q: 进步是真的吗？历史是在前进，还是循环、甚至退步？
debated.q_en: Is progress real? Is history moving forward, in cycles — or even backward?

debated.q: 现代的『文明进步』，是解放还是控制？
debated.q_en: Modern 'civilizational progress': liberation, or control?

debated.q: 容颜该顺其自然地老去，还是该努力医美、抗衰？
debated.q_en: Should we let our looks age naturally, or fight it with cosmetic work and anti-aging?

debated.q: AI 有没有、或可能有意识？我们又凭什么判断？
debated.q_en: Does (or could) AI have consciousness — and how would we ever know?

debated.q: 语言塑造思维吗？说不同语言的人，看到的是不同的世界吗？
debated.q_en: Does language shape thought? Do speakers of different languages see different worlds?

debated.q: 美，是主观感受，还是有客观的标准？
debated.q_en: Is beauty just in the eye of the beholder, or is there an objective standard?

debated.q: 我们为何系统性地低估『照护与情感劳动』的价值？（带孩子、陪伴、安抚、协调——这些撑起一切却没人记功的活）
debated.q_en: Why do we systematically undervalue care and emotional labor?

debated.q: 绩效考核与「赛马」（KPI、末位淘汰）是激励，还是毒药？
debated.q_en: Are performance metrics and forced ranking (KPIs, stack-ranking) a motivator, or a poison?

debated.q: 我们对远方陌生人的苦难，负有多大义务？
debated.q_en: How much do we owe the suffering of distant strangers?

debated.q: 拖延症，到底要不要治？
debated.q_en: Should we cure procrastination at all?

debated.q: 全球化正在让世界失去文化多样性吗？
debated.q_en: Is globalization costing us cultural diversity?

debated.q: 真爱是发现的，还是培养（甚至建构）出来的？
debated.q_en: Is true love found, or cultivated — even constructed?

debated.q: 公司到底该对谁负责——只对股东，还是也对员工与社会？
debated.q_en: Whom does a company answer to — only shareholders, or also its workers and society?

debated.q: 人真的在逃避自由吗？——自由是解放，还是一副人宁愿卸下的重担？
debated.q_en: Do humans really flee from freedom — is freedom liberation, or a burden people would rather set down?

debated.q: 该主动过「极简 / 少欲」的生活吗？
debated.q_en: Should we deliberately live simply?

debated.q: 「社会兴趣」是衡量活得好不好的尺吗？
debated.q_en: Is 'social interest' the yardstick of a life well lived?

debated.q: 濒死体验证明意识能脱离大脑吗？
debated.q_en: Do near-death experiences prove consciousness can leave the brain?

debated.q: 时间真的存在吗，还是一种幻觉？
debated.q_en: Does time really exist, or is it an illusion?

debated.q: 我们对地球（其他物种、后代）负有怎样的义务？
debated.q_en: What do we owe the Earth — other species, and future generations?

debated.q: 我们是不是正在失去『第三空间』？
debated.q_en: Are we losing our 'third places'?

debated.q: 该不该让算法来管人——派活、打分、监控，甚至解雇？
debated.q_en: Should algorithms manage people — assigning work, scoring, surveilling, even firing?

debated.q: 维系和谐，有时是否比说出真相更重要？（含：伪善是不是比赤裸的恶更可恨——道德表演与『人设』，究竟是文明的润滑剂还是腐蚀剂）
debated.q_en: Is keeping the peace sometimes more important than telling the truth? (Including: is hypocrisy more contemptible than open vice — is moral performance the lubricant of civilisation or its solvent?)

debated.q: 宇宙真的是「黑暗森林」吗？文明之间注定你死我活，还是可能合作？
debated.q_en: Is the universe really a 'dark forest'? Are civilizations doomed to mutual annihilation, or can they cooperate?

debated.q: 该不该用 AI「复活」逝去的亲人？
debated.q_en: Should you use AI to 'resurrect' a dead loved one?

debated.q: 自由与平等不可兼得时，该牺牲哪个？
debated.q_en: When liberty and equality cannot both be had, which gives way?

debated.q: 当 AI 比谁都懂，领导者还剩什么不可替代的？（含：最稀缺的会不会是『会读人』——读懂人、拿捏分寸、在冲突里维系信任的社会情感能力，机器能不能接管）
debated.q_en: When AI knows more than anyone, what is left that only a leader can do? (Including: will the scarcest skill turn out to be reading people — judging a face, calibrating tone, holding trust together through conflict — and can machines take that over?)

debated.q: 爱一个人，该介入他的人生多深？
debated.q_en: How far should love intervene in another's life?

debated.q: 该为过去的选择后悔吗？
debated.q_en: Should we regret the choices we made?

debated.q: 真的存在平行宇宙吗？
debated.q_en: Do parallel universes really exist?

debated.q: 有什么是金钱不该买卖的？
debated.q_en: Is there anything money should not be able to buy?

debated.q: 职场该不该表达野心？
debated.q_en: Should you show your ambition at work?

debated.q: 园丁还是木匠？——父母该「雕琢」孩子，还是营造环境让他自己长成？
debated.q_en: Gardener or carpenter — should parents shape the child, or cultivate the soil and let them grow unpredictably?

debated.q: 真正的『勇气』是什么？
debated.q_en: What is courage, really?

debated.q: 世界是唯物的，还是唯心的？
debated.q_en: Is the world made of matter, or of mind?

debated.q: 物质极度丰裕后，人会走向衰亡吗？
debated.q_en: Does material abundance lead to decline?

debated.q: AI 做完入门的活，新人怎么学本事？
debated.q_en: If AI does the entry-level work, how do novices learn?

debated.q: 忠诚该不该被考验？
debated.q_en: Should loyalty be tested — and is a trust that holds only while unverified really trust at all?

debated.q: 钱该省下来滚复利，还是该花掉？
debated.q_en: Should money be saved to compound, or spent?

debated.q: AI 能伪造一切，我们还信什么？
debated.q_en: When AI can fake anything, what is left to trust?

debated.q: 社会该不该允许安乐死与协助死亡？
debated.q_en: Should society allow euthanasia and assisted dying?

debated.q: 只有一条晋升阶梯的组织，浪费了谁？
debated.q_en: Who is wasted by an organisation with only one ladder?

debated.q: 趁年轻，该搏事业还是先去看世界？
debated.q_en: When young: build a career, or go see the world first?

debated.q: 该不该原谅伤害过你的人？
debated.q_en: Should you forgive someone who has wronged you?

debated.q: 理性与信仰冲突时，该让哪一个让步？
debated.q_en: When reason and faith collide, which should yield?

debated.q: 该不该吃肉？动物有没有值得我们尊重的道德地位？
debated.q_en: Should we eat meat? Do animals have a moral standing we're bound to respect?

debated.q: 你的工作是真被需要，还是被造出来的？
debated.q_en: Is your job actually needed, or was it invented?

debated.q: 该给关系做减法吗？
debated.q_en: Should you prune your relationships?

debated.q: 该不该信命？算命、八字、星座为何长盛不衰
debated.q_en: Should you believe in fate? Why do fortune-telling and astrology endure

debated.q: 凡事都追求『最优／高效』，是不是正在系统性地掏空我们的韧性？
debated.q_en: By chasing 'optimal' and 'efficient' in everything, are we systematically hollowing out our resilience?

debated.q: 民主一定是最好的制度吗？
debated.q_en: Is democracy necessarily the best system?

debated.q: 监控为什么总是朝下查？
debated.q_en: Why does scrutiny always run downhill?

debated.q: 仪式还有用吗？
debated.q_en: Do rituals still do anything?

debated.q: 「工作与生活的平衡」真的存在吗？
debated.q_en: Is work-life balance a real thing?

debated.q: 我们记得的过去，有多少是重新编造的？
debated.q_en: How much of the past we remember was rebuilt on the spot

debated.q: 死刑该废除吗？
debated.q_en: Should the death penalty be abolished?

debated.q: 上班的地方，为什么不投票？
debated.q_en: Why is there no vote where we work?

debated.q: 该不该把家底留给孩子？
debated.q_en: Should you leave your wealth to your children?

debated.q: 精神痛苦是脑病，还是正常反应？
debated.q_en: Is mental suffering a brain disease or a normal response?

debated.q: 机遇和位置，比努力更重要吗？
debated.q_en: Do opportunity and position matter more than effort?

debated.q: 有没有人类永远想不明白的事？
debated.q_en: Are there things humans can never understand?

debated.q: 为了公共健康，国家能管到哪一步？
debated.q_en: How far may the state go for the sake of public health?

debated.q: 时势造英雄，还是英雄挑对了时势？
debated.q_en: Do the times make the hero, or does the hero pick the right times?

debated.q: 审慎是行动的敌人吗？
debated.q_en: Is deliberation the enemy of action?

debated.q: 该去带人，还是把手艺做深？
debated.q_en: Should you manage people, or go deeper into the craft?

debated.q: 关系是谁在维护？
debated.q_en: Who does the work of keeping people together?

debated.q: 有没有放之四海皆准的美德？
debated.q_en: Are there virtues that hold everywhere?

debated.q: 钱、婚姻、国界，是真实的东西吗？
debated.q_en: Are money, marriage and borders real things?

debated.q: 一个人的优点和缺点，是不是同一个特点的两面？
debated.q_en: Are a person's strengths and flaws two faces of the same trait

debated.q: 有些工作会把人改掉吗？
debated.q_en: Do some jobs change the person doing them?

debated.q: 生活里的『偶遇』正在消失吗？
debated.q_en: Are chance encounters disappearing from our lives?

debated.q: 外貌在多大程度上是一种『资本』？
debated.q_en: How far are looks a form of capital?

debated.q: 一件事被解释清楚，就变得不值钱了吗？
debated.q_en: Does explaining something drain the value out of it?

debated.q: 谁还愿意对你说真话？
debated.q_en: Who is still willing to tell you the truth?

debated.q: 一旦拿来考核，好指标就坏了吗？
debated.q_en: Does a good measure spoil the moment you grade people by it?

debated.q: 父母偏心，能不能说出口？
debated.q_en: Can a family admit to having a favourite child?

debated.q: 当『裁员』改叫『优化』，我们还判断得了吗？
debated.q_en: When layoffs are renamed optimization, can we still judge?

debated.q: 梦是内心的密电，还是大脑随手编的故事？
debated.q_en: Are dreams a coded message from within, or a story the brain improvises?

debated.q: 该磨自己，还是换个地方？
debated.q_en: Grind at yourself, or change where you stand?

debated.q: 职业思维该不该带回家？
debated.q_en: Should your professional mindset come home with you?

debated.q: 没共同经历的人，还能互相理解吗？
debated.q_en: Can people who share no experience understand each other?

debated.q: 谁有权拿别人的人生下注？
debated.q_en: Who is entitled to bet other people's lives?

debated.q: 跨学科的「思维模型」是智慧还是半吊子？
debated.q_en: Cross-disciplinary 'mental models': wisdom, or a half-trained amateur?

debated.q: 能扛的人，是不是总被多派活？
debated.q_en: Does being the one who copes just get you more work?

debated.q: 说不出来的本事，能被教会吗？
debated.q_en: Can know-how that cannot be put into words be taught?

debated.q: 人生的几个时钟对不上，该迁就哪一个？
debated.q_en: When your several clocks fall out of phase, which one do you obey?

debated.q: 我们该为上一代做过的事负责吗？
debated.q_en: Are we answerable for what earlier generations did?

debated.q: 太不可替代的人，反而升不上去吗？
debated.q_en: Does being irreplaceable keep you from moving up?

debated.q: 一个决定，该按当时的信息还是按结果来评？
debated.q_en: Should a decision be judged on the information then, or on how it turned out?

debated.q: 人是怎么一步步走到当初绝不会做的事的？
debated.q_en: How does a person arrive, step by step, at what they would once never have done?

debated.q: 还有没有不被看见的地方？
debated.q_en: Is there anywhere left that is not watched?

debated.q: 不用钱来分，就更公平吗？
debated.q_en: Is sharing things out without money any fairer?

debated.q: 你所在的组织，正处在它的哪一段？
debated.q_en: Which stage of its own life is your organization in?

debated.q: 没有大脑，也能「想」吗？
debated.q_en: Can there be thinking without a brain?
